newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia moving into lower rates era - Howard.
newsitem.headline: Australia moving into lower rates era - Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday the economy was entering an era of lower interest rates and he would work to reinforce lower interest rates through lower inflation.
"I think you're getting into an era of lower interest rates in Australia," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE.

Asked if Australia should return to an era where the Reserve Bank and government-owned banks subsidised interest rates to create employment, Howard said he was more attracted to bringing rates down by lowering budget deficits.

"I'm far more attracted to getting the budget deficit down, building up good surpluses, making other changes to the economy and reinforcing those lower interest rates via lower inflation," Howard said.
Howard said he had to be careful about what he said about interest rates, given his comments on Tuesday had sparked lower market interest rates and a lower Australian dollar.

"The reductions in interest rates that have occurred have been very, very good, and I hope that over a period of time -- and I've got to be careful what I say here because the other day I expressed the sort of normal aspirations that any prime minister would express and that is you want to have lower interest rates and the money markets reacted in a particular fashion," he said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia, which has an agreement with the government to act independently, last cut official interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent on May 23.
Economists believe there is a good chance the Reserve Bank will cut official rates again within the next two months.
